# Indonesia

Everything this library holds for Indonesia, with provenance. Tilt = OLS slope of ln(rate) on wealth rank 0–1; ogcore consumes tilt ÷ 100 (see [AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md)).

## DHS survey gradients (fertility & child mortality)

From [`data/gradient_library_latest.csv`](../../data/gradient_library_latest.csv) (most recent survey; the full survey history is in `gradient_library.csv`).

| Indicator | Survey year | Tilt | Poorest/richest | Q1 … Q5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|

Source: DHS Program indicator API (wealth-quintile breakdown); tilt = OLS slope of ln(rate) on wealth rank.

## Adult-mortality route for calibration

No census household-deaths module exists, so use the [general gradient](../methods/general-gradient.md): at GNI per capita ≈ $5,010 (~2024), predicted tilt(45q15) = **−0.79** ± 0.16, spread across age bands with the by-age offsets in `data/general_gradient.csv`.

## Provenance notes

- No census household-deaths module is available, so there is no measured adult-mortality gradient; use the general gradient (worked value below). The DHS rows (IDHS 2017) cover fertility and child mortality directly.
- Indonesia is the canonical tempo case: its TFR-by-wealth gradient is nearly flat while adolescent childbearing differs ~8× between poorest and richest quintiles — the gradient lives in the age pattern, not the total.
